$schema_note: Each template defines: which grades it applies to, parameters sampled at generation time, generation constraints, distractor rules (for choice-based interactions), grading rules, and hint policy. 'pool:' references point into knowledge-base.json grade_scopes (cumulative). One worked example instance is embedded per core template.

srs_tags: skill atoms for spaced repetition, e.g. key_sig:Eb_major, note_read:bass:ledger_below

generation_rules: Sample pitch uniformly over the grade's range; from G2 boost ledger-line pitches to 40% weight (they are the new material)
From G4, alto-clef items get 50% weight while the clef is new; from G5 same for tenor
Render as a semibreve unless testing duration too
distractor_rules: the name the note would have in the 'other' clef (clef-confusion distractor)
templates.grading: case-insensitive letter name; accidental must be included if present

example.prompt: Write the name of this note.

generation_rules: Total must equal exactly one legal note value (possibly dotted) in the grade scope
Subtraction allowed from G1; double-dot operands from G4; triplet-value questions from G2
Reject trivial identities (x + 0), duplicates of recent items
distractor_rules: value one step longer/shorter on the note tree
the un-dotted version of the correct dotted answer

example.prompt: Answer this musical sum with one note: crotchet + quaver = ?
hints: Use the note tree: a crotchet is worth two quavers.

generation_rules: Generate 4-6 bars in one time signature from grade scope; corrupt 40-60% of them by +/- one small value or a wrong rest
From G3, corruptions may involve compound-time beat maths; from G5, irregular metres
Generate melody via melody_generator (see spec doc §4) so every bar sums exactly; strip internal barlines
If anacrusis: first partial bar + final bar must sum to one whole bar
Beaming must already be correct so grouping is a usable clue (books rely on this)
hints: Look at how the notes are grouped - beams show you where the beats are.

generation_rules: Generate 1-2 bars with unambiguous grouping; ensure exactly one grade-scope signature fits (e.g. avoid a bar readable as both 3/4 and 6/8 unless beaming disambiguates - the 6/8 vs 3/4 contrast IS the intended G3 difficulty)
distractor_rules: same total, different beat unit (3/4 vs 6/8 vs 3/2)

generation_rules: Generate a correctly-summing rhythm written with wrong/no beaming; learner regroups per beaming_rules_by_time_signature
templates.grading: accept any beaming listed as legal for that signature in knowledge-base (e.g. 4/4 quavers in 2s or beat-pair 4s); reject beams across the middle of a 4/4 bar

generation_rules: Generate a bar missing rest(s) at a marked position; required silence = signature total minus sounding values
Compound time (G3+): rests must show each dotted-crotchet beat correctly; G4+ may require double-dotted rests
templates.grading: accept all conventional decompositions defined in beaming/rest rules; canonical answer shown in feedback

templates.interaction: mcq (rendered key signatures) | text_input (name the key)
distractor_rules: correct accidentals, wrong stave positions (the books' favourite trap)
for 'name the key': the relative major/minor of the answer (from G2), the enharmonic equivalent (from G5: F# vs Gb)
templates.grading: for name-the-key with a bare key signature, require the melody/tonic context OR accept both relative answers and teach the distinction in feedback

example.prompt: Tick the correctly written key signature of E flat major.
distractors: Bb Eb Ab with Ab misplaced an octave

templates.interaction: stave_input | mcq (spot the wrong note) | multi_select (mark semitone pairs)

parameters.key+form: pool: majors; harmonic minor G2+; melodic asc/desc G3+; chromatic G4+

generation_rules: Build from scale_patterns in knowledge-base; corrupt exactly one note for spot-the-error variants
Melodic minor items must state direction; descending uses natural form
Chromatic scale grading: enforce the 'no letter name more than twice in succession' rule
templates.srs_tags_rule: tag by key AND form so weak scales resurface individually

generation_rules: G1-3: answer by number. G4+: technical names from knowledge-base degree_names; include raised-7th context in minors
distractor_rules: the degree the note would be in the relative key

templates.interaction: mcq | text_input | stave_input (write a note to form the interval)

parameters.per_grade_scope: G1-2 number only above tonic; G3 +type above tonic; G4 any two diatonic notes, +aug/dim; G5 any notes, +compound, any clef, with/without key signature

generation_rules: Sample lower note per scope; upper note within scope's max span
For write-the-note variants, specify 'higher than the given note' (as the books do) to make the answer unique
G5: 20% of items compound; 20% in alto/tenor clefs
distractor_rules: simple name for a compound interval

parameters.chord: G1-3 tonic triad; G4 I/IV/V root; G5 I/II/IV/V + inversions

generation_rules: Build triads by stacking 3rds from the scale (harmonic form in minors)
G5 inversion items: label with number+letter (e.g. IIb); offer the book's grid method as a hint scaffold
distractor_rules: triad of the dominant/subdominant instead of tonic

generation_rules: Generate 1-2 bar melody; require rewrite one octave up/down into a specified clef (treble<->bass G3; +alto G4; any pair G5)
templates.grading: every note must match target pitch exactly; rhythm must be preserved; key signature must be rewritten for the new clef

parameters.context: abstract melody | transposing instrument (Bb/A/F) to/from concert pitch

generation_rules: Source melody 1-2 bars, may include accidentals outside the key (the G5 book drills this)
Grading checks: new key signature correct, every note correct, accidentals correctly respelled
Instrument variant: state the instrument and direction explicitly (the exam gives the interval)
Generate a 2-4 bar melody whose final two melody notes are chord tones of the target cadence pair (V-I perfect, IV-I plagal, ?-V imperfect)
Every boxed melody note must belong to at least one chord from {I, II, IV, V}; ensure the intended answer is unambiguous at the final pair
templates.grading: each box: accept any chord from {I,II,IV,V} containing the melody note UNLESS it breaks the named cadence at the final pair; cadence name graded strictly
hints: Check which chords contain the melody note, then choose the pair that makes the required cadence.

generation_rules: Sample from cumulative deck (terms-signs-deck.json) weighted by SRS due-ness
Both directions: term->meaning and meaning->term
Distractors from the SAME category (a tempo term's distractors are tempo terms) - this mirrors the books and is what makes items discriminating
Include abbreviation/sign variants (rall., D.C., the cresc. hairpin) as separate SRS atoms
G4: recognition only - show sign, name it (trill, turn, upper/lower mordent, acciaccatura, appoggiatura)
G5: show a written-out ornament figure; learner selects/places the correct sign. NEVER the reverse (sign->written-out) - the syllabus explicitly excludes it
Facts pool: families (strings/woodwind/brass/percussion + voice types at G5), clefs used, sound production, standard directions; transposing status feeds interval_transposition items

COMPOSITE: generate (or select from public-domain corpus at G4-5) an 8-16 bar passage within grade scope, decorated with grade-scope terms, dynamics, articulation and (G4+) ornaments and instrument labels

Then instantiate 4-7 sub-questions from these atoms: find-the-bar (contains tonic triad / dotted quaver / interval X), longest/shortest/highest/lowest note, degree of a marked note, TRUE/FALSE about markings, bar-comparison (same pitches/rhythm as bar N), meaning-in-context of a term, (G4-5) instrument questions, (G5) two-stave comparison for piano or violin+piano textures
Sub-question answers must be verified against the generated score programmatically - never hand-waved
templates.grading: per-sub-question; unit mastery requires >=80% across the flow
